assignments.text:
Between this soft
and yielding foundation of her life upon which she
could find no firm footing, and the rock of Catherine
Vernon who remained quite immovable and uninfluenced
by her, coming no nearer as the years went
on, yet hemming in her steps and lessening her
freedom, the conditions of existence seemed all
against the high-spirited, ambitious, active-minded
and impatient girl, with her warm affections, and
quick intelligence, and hasty disposition.
assignments.summary: Hester is trapped between her weak mother and the unyielding Catherine Vernon, her ambition and energy constrained by these two opposing forces.
assignments.best_quote: Between this soft and yielding foundation of her life upon which she could find no firm footing, and the rock of Catherine Vernon who remained quite immovable and uninfluenced by her, coming no nearer as the years went on, yet hemming in her steps and lessening her freedom, the conditions of existence seemed all against the high-spirited, ambitious, active-minded and impatient girl

assignments.text:
When an individual feels capable of
performing the part of a visible Providence, it
becomes incumbent upon that person, so far as
possible, to know everything, to shut his eyes to no
detail, to note every little incident, and to encourage [Pg 203] 
not only the confidences of his possible clients and
 protégés , but the observations of all surrounding them,
and every hint as to their motives, their intentions
and purposes, that can be got at.
assignments.summary: The narrator satirizes how Catherine's self-image as a benevolent Providence justifies her intrusive knowledge-gathering about everyone around her.
assignments.best_quote: When an individual feels capable of performing the part of a visible Providence, it becomes incumbent upon that person, so far as possible, to know everything.

assignments.text:
It cannot be denied that this was to some
extent the tone unconsciously adopted by Catherine
in her dealings with the poor relations who were so
largely indebted to her bounty. There was a great
deal that was ridiculous in their little affectations
and discontents, and the half-resentment, half-exaction
with which they received her benefits.
assignments.summary: The ridiculous affectations of the poor relations could have made Catherine misanthropic, but instead cultivated cynicism and contemptuous tolerance.

assignments.text:
What an extraordinary shock
would it have been for his companion, who felt
herself to sit in the place of the audience, seeing
the puppets play their pranks upon the stage and
exhibit all their fooleries, to know that she herself
was the actor, turned outside in and seen through
in all her devices, to this boy whom she loved!
assignments.summary: The narrator delivers a brilliant ironic revelation: Catherine believes herself the audience observing the foolish actors of her little world, but is actually the actor being observed and judged by Edward, whom she loves.
assignments.best_quote: What an extraordinary shock would it have been for his companion, who felt herself to sit in the place of the audience, seeing the puppets play their pranks upon the stage and exhibit all their fooleries, to know that she herself was the actor, turned outside in and seen through in all her devices, to this boy whom she loved!

assignments.text:
The outside crowd,
knowing nothing of the meaning of these investigations,
is apt to mistake them altogether; but
Catherine did not care much about the outside world. It was her wish that everything should be told her,
and she was perhaps too apt to think that those who
were not willing or able to open their hearts, were
people who had secrets in their life, and probably a
good deal that would not bear the light.
assignments.summary: Catherine dismisses the outside world's judgment and assumes anyone unwilling to confide in her must be hiding something shameful.
assignments.best_quote: Those who were not willing or able to open their hearts, were people who had secrets in their life, and probably a good deal that would not bear the light.

assignments.text:
The sisters immediately plunged
into that "criticism of life" which could scarcely be
called poetry, in their hands.
assignments.summary: The sisters are about to engage in gossip, which the narrator sardonically describes as criticism.
assignments.best_quote: that 'criticism of life' which could scarcely be called poetry, in their hands

assignments.text:
"I don't think that is my experience. My old
people are very indulgent; but then, I am a mere
visitor. Home does not mean much to me," said
Ashton. If he had been in the presence of any lady
he would have sighed as he said this—being in
absolute freedom with one of his own kind he smiled,
and it was Edward who sighed.
assignments.summary: The narrator notes that Ashton would perform melancholy for ladies but reveals his true indifference with Edward, whose sigh betrays his contrary emotional depth.
assignments.best_quote: If he had been in the presence of any lady he would have sighed as he said this—being in absolute freedom with one of his own kind he smiled, and it was Edward who sighed.

assignments.text:
She
was intended to laugh, indeed, if they did not secure
another sentiment; but the first aim, and perhaps
the last aim, of the insidious Roland, had been to [Pg 79] 
secure this other sentiment. Hester did not enter
into these distinctions, but she felt them; and when
she thus put forward Mrs. Morgan's failing sight, it
was with a natural casuistry which she knew would
be partially seen through, and yet would have its
effect.
assignments.summary: The narrator explains that Roland's true aim beneath the humor was to secure genuine romantic sentiment, and that Hester deployed conscious casuistry in her defense, knowing it would be partially transparent yet effective.
assignments.best_quote: She was intended to laugh, indeed, if they did not secure another sentiment; but the first aim, and perhaps the last aim, of the insidious Roland, had been to secure this other sentiment. Hester did not enter into these distinctions, but she felt them; and when she thus put forward Mrs. Morgan's failing sight, it was with a natural casuistry which she knew would be partially seen through, and yet would have its effect.

assignments.text:
The rage with which she would
contemplate herself when she yielded to the first
temptation and launched at Cousin Catherine in a
moment of passion one of those arrows which were
manufactured in the Vernonry, the deep disgust
which would fill her when she felt herself, like
Catherine, contemplating the world from a pinnacle
of irony, chill but smiling, swept her young spirit
like tempests. To grow at all in the midst of such
gales and whirlwinds was something.
assignments.summary: Hester's self-reproach for moments of cruelty to Catherine and adoption of Catherine's cynicism sweeps over her like violent storms, causing deep psychological turmoil.
assignments.best_quote: The rage with which she would contemplate herself when she yielded to the first temptation and launched at Cousin Catherine in a moment of passion one of those arrows which were manufactured in the Vernonry, the deep disgust which would fill her when she felt herself, like Catherine, contemplating the world from a pinnacle of irony, chill but smiling, swept her young spirit like tempests.

assignments.text: "Do you?"
assignments.summary: Hester confesses her desire for achievement and renown: to be born to greatness or to earn her own significance.
assignments.best_quote: I should like to be a king's daughter or a great soldier's or a great statesman's. I should like my name to mean something. I should like people to say, when they hear it, that is——

assignments.text:
It was not
to be expected that she could grow otherwise than
contorted with the blasts. She came to the flower
and bloom of existence with a heart made to believe
and trust, yet warped to almost all around, and
finding no spot of honest standing-ground on which
to trust herself.
assignments.summary: Hester enters young adulthood with a capacity for belief but warped by her corrupting environment, unable to find solid moral ground.
assignments.best_quote: She came to the flower and bloom of existence with a heart made to believe and trust, yet warped to almost all around, and finding no spot of honest standing-ground on which to trust herself.

assignments.text:
Hester kept gazing through that wintry blackness,
with eyes still wide open, and her clear brows
puckered with wonder and alarm. Was it natural,
then, a thing she could accept as just, that it was
enough for her to sympathise, to share the consequences,
to stand by the chief actor whatever happened,
but never to share in the initiative or have [Pg 125] 
any moral concern in the motive or the means of
what was done?
assignments.summary: Hester questions whether women's prescribed role—to sympathize and share consequences but never to understand or influence the action—is just or natural.
assignments.best_quote: Was it natural, then, a thing she could accept as just, that it was enough for her to sympathise, to share the consequences, to stand by the chief actor whatever happened, but never to share in the initiative or have any moral concern in the motive or the means of what was done?

assignments.text:
Her breast swelled, her breath came short with an
impulse of impatience and longing to have such an
opportunity, to show the mettle that was in her. But how could she do it? Catherine was rich, but
Hester was poor. In this way she was diverted for
the moment from her anxiety.
assignments.summary: Hester's desire to act heroically is constrained by her poverty, which denies her the resources Catherine possessed.
assignments.best_quote: Her breast swelled, her breath came short with an impulse of impatience and longing to have such an opportunity...But how could she do it? Catherine was rich, but Hester was poor

assignments.text:
The papers he was
examining he had brought himself in a black bag
from the safe in the bank. He had locked the black
bag into an old oak escritoire till after dinner. He
was looking over them now with the greatest care,
and a face full of suppressed, but almost solemn
excitement. They were securities of all kinds, and
meant an amount of money which went to Edward's
head even more than the chances of fortune.
assignments.summary: Edward examines securities stolen from the bank safe with suppressed excitement, intoxicated by the amount of money they represent.
assignments.best_quote: The papers he was examining he had brought himself in a black bag from the safe in the bank. He had locked the black bag into an old oak escritoire till after dinner. He was looking over them now with the greatest care, and a face full of suppressed, but almost solemn excitement. They were securities of all kinds, and meant an amount of money which went to Edward's head even more than the chances of fortune

assignments.text:
All [Pg 37] 
that in his power; no chance of being called upon to
produce them, or to render an account of the stewardship
which had been so freely committed to him! It
was enough to make any man's head go round.
assignments.summary: Edward realizes that as a trusted steward of the bank's securities, no one will question his management, and this absolute power intoxicates him.
assignments.best_quote: All that in his power; no chance of being called upon to produce them, or to render an account of the stewardship which had been so freely committed to him! It was enough to make any man's head go round

assignments.text:
"You could do nothing less: but I cannot be
different here. Suspicion produces treachery, don't
you know?" he said, with his face close to her ear. "I cannot be true here. No, don't say anything. I ought, but I cannot. It is in the air. All of us,
every one except you, we are making believe and
finding each other out, yet going on all the same.
assignments.summary: Edward confesses his inability to be true to himself under Catherine's watch, describing the pervasive atmosphere of insincerity and suspicion she creates.
assignments.best_quote: I cannot be different here. Suspicion produces treachery, don't you know? I cannot be true here. No, don't say anything. I ought, but I cannot. It is in the air. All of us, every one except you, we are making believe and finding each other out, yet going on all the same.

assignments.text:
In this way the spring went on. It had appeared
to Edward himself as certain that some great  coup 
must have settled his fate long before. It was his
inexperience, perhaps, and the excitement of his
determination to act for himself, which had made
everything appear so imminent; but after all it did
not turn out so. The course of events went on in
that leisurely current which is far more deadly in its
sweep than any sudden cataract.
assignments.summary: Edward's financial ventures proceed gradually and indecisively, with neither clear gain nor catastrophic loss, but slow accumulation of danger.
assignments.best_quote: The course of events went on in that leisurely current which is far more deadly in its sweep than any sudden cataract.

assignments.text:
Had there been only the risks of the crisis, the
meeting of alarmed and anxious creditors, the chance
even of criminal prosecution, he might have faced it;
but to return again to that old routine, to take up
his former life, was impossible. He flew along like
the wind. There was still an hour or more before
the train would start. Would the women gather
themselves together, he wondered, soon enough to
send after him, to prevent his journey?
assignments.summary: Edward reflects that he might have faced financial ruin and prosecution, but cannot bear to return to his ordinary former life; he resolves to walk to the train junction.
assignments.best_quote: Had there been only the risks of the crisis, the meeting of alarmed and anxious creditors, the chance even of criminal prosecution, he might have faced it; but to return again to that old routine, to take up his former life, was impossible.

assignments.text:
"A
man requires a great deal of original impulse before
he will go the length of murder. The other has a
milder but similar attraction; you ruin other people,
which shakes them up, and gives a change of air."
assignments.summary: Edward elaborates that bankruptcy, though milder than murder, offers similar appeal—it disrupts others' lives and provides the excitement of upheaval.
assignments.best_quote: A man requires a great deal of original impulse before he will go the length of murder. The other has a milder but similar attraction; you ruin other people, which shakes them up, and gives a change of air.

assignments.text:
She did not desire to
be turned from the comedy which she had in her
way enjoyed for years, seeing through, as she said, all
the little world of dependents that hung about her,
drawing out their weaknesses, perceiving the bitter
grudge that lay under their exterior of smiles, and
the thousand ways in which they made up to themselves
for the humiliation of being in her debt—in
order to turn to what might prove the less amusing
contemplation of her own weaknesses, or recognise
the element of evil in that which was certainly not
amusing.
assignments.summary: The narrator reveals Catherine's determination not to turn from her enjoyment of observing others' weaknesses and self-interest, preferring not to examine her own nature or recognize the evil in her judgement.
assignments.best_quote: She did not desire to be turned from the comedy which she had in her way enjoyed for years, seeing through, as she said, all the little world of dependents that hung about her, drawing out their weaknesses, perceiving the bitter grudge that lay under their exterior of smiles, and the thousand ways in which they made up to themselves for the humiliation of being in her debt—in order to turn to what might prove the less amusing contemplation of her own weaknesses, or recognise the element of evil in that which was certainly not amusing.

assignments.text:
She showed no feeling
about it, people said; and indeed Catherine felt
that neither about this nor any other external thing
was she capable of showing much feeling. She cared
nothing about leaving the Grange. Had she been
actually brought down as far as the almshouse, in all
likelihood she would have taken it with the proudest [Pg 259] 
placidity. What was there in that to move a soul?
assignments.summary: Catherine shows no sentiment about leaving the Grange or selling its contents, viewing material possessions as inconsequential to a person of her philosophical temperament.
assignments.best_quote: Had she been actually brought down as far as the almshouse, in all likelihood she would have taken it with the proudest placidity.

assignments.text:
The
windows were all closed, and candles upon the table
still burning: but the light swept in from above, over
the top of the shutters, which were not so high as the
glass, and lighted up the room in a strange abstract
way like a studio or a prison.
assignments.summary: The room is lit by a strange mixture of candlelight and dawn light, creating an abstract, prison-like or studio atmosphere.
assignments.best_quote: The windows were all closed, and candles upon the table still burning: but the light swept in from above, over the top of the shutters...lighted up the room in a strange abstract way like a studio or a prison.

assignments.text:
There were not even any heavings
and groanings, like those that warn the surrounding
country before a volcano bursts forth. Nevertheless,
this girl, who had been so long a spectator, [Pg 22] 
pushed aside from the action about her, but with
the keen sight of injured pride and wounded feeling,
seeing the secret thread of meaning that ran
through everything, felt premonitions, she could not
tell how, in the heated air, and through the
domestic calm.
assignments.summary: The narrator eloquently describes Hester's sensitive perception of imminent crisis; despite outward calm, she senses approaching danger like a volcano about to erupt, perceiving hidden meaning beneath surface tranquility.
assignments.best_quote: All was still, and everything going on in its calm habitual way. There were not even any heavings and groanings, like those that warn the surrounding country before a volcano bursts forth. Nevertheless, this girl, who had been so long a spectator, pushed aside from the action about her, but with the keen sight of injured pride and wounded feeling, seeing the secret thread of meaning that ran through everything, felt premonitions, she could not tell how, in the heated air, and through the domestic calm.

assignments.text:
Through Catherine's mind at that moment there ran
the whole story of her later days, how she had used
herself to the pretences of all about her, how every
one around had taken from her, and snarled at her,
eaten of her bread, and drunk of her cup, and hated [Pg 186] 
her—except Edward. He alone had been her prop,
her religion of the affections.
assignments.summary: Catherine's entire adult life has been consumed by serving others who exploited her; only Edward seemed to reciprocate her devotion.
assignments.best_quote: everyone around had taken from her, and snarled at her, eaten of her bread, and drunk of her cup, and hated her—except Edward.

assignments.text:
It was scarcely
one o'clock, but in summer there is little night, and
already the air had begun to whiten with some premonition
of day. She held up her face to the sky—an
old face, with so many lines in it, suddenly [Pg 198] 
smitten as with a death-blow. Her eyes, under the
curve of pain, which makes the eyelids quiver, looked
up to the pale skies with what is the last appeal of
humanity.
assignments.summary: As dawn breaks, Catherine lifts her aged, grief-stricken face to the paling sky in a gesture of ultimate human appeal and anguish.
assignments.best_quote: Her eyes, under the curve of pain, which makes the eyelids quiver, looked up to the pale skies with what is the last appeal of humanity.

assignments.text:
For why?—for why?—an honest life, an
honourable career, a soul that had shrunk from no
labour or pain, a hand that never had been closed to
human distress—and repaid with misery at the end! Is there no reason in it when God's creature lifts a
face of anguish to His throne, and asks why? She
paused on the threshold of her house, which was
desolate, and made that mute appeal.
assignments.summary: Catherine's unspoken lament questions divine justice: after a lifetime of honest, laborious virtue and compassion, why is she repaid with misery?
assignments.best_quote: Is there no reason in it when God's creature lifts a face of anguish to His throne, and asks why?

assignments.text:
The question as to
how the bank came into that peril, the suspicion
that her father must have been somehow connected
with it, the heat of her research after the key of the
mystery, faded away for the moment in a vague,
general excitement and eager yet vain desire to have
it in her power to do something, she also——a
desire which many a young mind has felt as well
as Hester; to have that golden opportunity—the
occasion to do a heroic deed, to save some one, to
venture your own life, to escape the bonds of every
day, and once have a chance of showing what was in
you!
assignments.summary: Hester's yearning for the heroic opportunity to transcend her limited circumstances distracts her from anxiety about her father.
assignments.best_quote: a desire which many a young mind has felt as well as Hester; to have that golden opportunity—the occasion to do a heroic deed, to save some one, to venture your own life, to escape the bonds of every day, and once have a chance of showing what was in you!

assignments.text:
And the silence resumed its sway. She laid
herself back as before—her pale head against the
dark curtains stood out like ivory. Some time
afterwards she sighed two or three times heavily,
then there was no sound at all. The fire burned
cheerfully, the lamp shed its steady glow upon
Hester's book, to which after this talk she did not,
as may be supposed, pay very much attention.
assignments.summary: Catherine lays back with her pale head against dark curtains and becomes still. Hours pass as Hester reads, then a supernatural chill sweeps through the warm room as Hester realises Catherine's hands have grown cold.
assignments.best_quote: her pale head against the dark curtains stood out like ivory. Some time afterwards she sighed two or three times heavily, then there was no sound at all... A chill crept into the room like nothing Hester had ever felt before, though all was still, serenely warm and bright to outward appearance.

assignments.text:
Her last stronghold had fallen. This it
is which makes calamity so terrible to the old. She
could not get beyond it. There was nothing, nothing
in her path but this, blocking it across with a darkness
that would never be dispersed. If he had died
she would have known she could not remain long
behind him, and the gloom would have been but a
mist between; but he had not died.
assignments.summary: Catherine's final defences have crumbled; she faces a darkness that ageing offers no comfort in escaping, unable to imagine endurance.
assignments.best_quote: Her last stronghold had fallen. This it is which makes calamity so terrible to the old. She could not get beyond it.

assignments.text:
It was not for this sort of trifling work
that he had set himself to watch those fluctuations,
which are more delicate than anything in nature
they could be compared to. The blowing of the
winds and their changes were prose compared to
the headlong poetry of the money-market. Edward
felt so many new pulses waking in him, such a
hurrying fever in his veins, that he could not control
himself.
assignments.summary: Edward feels awakening excitement at the delicate fluctuations of the money market, which he compares to poetry rather than prose.
assignments.best_quote: The blowing of the winds and their changes were prose compared to the headlong poetry of the money-market.

assignments.text:
And, indeed, his
mind had gone further than his practice, and had [Pg 24] 
reached a point of excitement at which the boundaries
of right and wrong become so indistinct as to
exert little, if any, control over either the conscience
or the imagination.
assignments.summary: Edward's mental state has reached dangerous heights where moral boundaries have become blurred and ineffective.
assignments.best_quote: his mind had gone further than his practice, and had reached a point of excitement at which the boundaries of right and wrong become so indistinct as to exert little, if any, control over either the conscience or the imagination

assignments.text:
The most wonderful complication of all, the companionship
in which he had left England, was not
told to her then. It threw to all the others a
horrible mockery upon the whole story.
assignments.summary: The narrator hints at a remarkable discovery: Edward's companion in his departure from England, a detail kept from Catherine initially.
assignments.best_quote: The most wonderful complication of all, the companionship in which he had left England, was not told to her then.
